# KB3d: the `(11,6)/(6,11)` remainder rows `(5,1),(6,0)` of the 17-point cover question — impossible by an exact Fourier/Parseval identity (no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson), universality of a restored seven-source singleton word is the covering condition `P + P = F2^7` on its prefix set. [PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542) by Aaron Wang asserts **"No 17-point set covers `F2^7`"**. [PR 2773](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2773) by Aaron Wang audited that claim at the set level and recorded the whole remainder: the rows `(5,1),(6,0)` of the `(11,6)/(6,11)` family (pair-sum excess 5 and 6 at 11 points, `shared = 1`, `c = 1`), mattering only at `L = 22`. This package decides those two rows.

**Result (set level; no words enumerated; labels in `CERTIFICATE.json`):**

- **PROVEN**: rows `(5,1)` and `(6,0)` are impossible. An exact Fourier/Parseval identity on the forced odd-coverage profile excludes the entire `(11,6)/(6,11)` family: for a set `A` in the even coset and `B` in the odd coset of `F2^7` with sizes 11 and 6 (either order), the 66 cross sums cannot cover the 64 odd masks. Exact obstruction in both orders: Parseval remainder 696 versus allowed 504, deficit 192.
- **PROVEN** (jointly with PR 2542 and PR 2773): "No 17-point set covers `F2^7`" is complete at the set level — all six counting-feasible splits are excluded. Consequently at `L = 22` every universal word needs at least 18 distinct prefixes.
- **CHECKED**: the recorded predecessor anchors are reproduced before any new number (table below; commands and outputs in `ANCHOR-REPRO.json`).
- **DEMOTED**: the construction route (an 11-set of pair-sum excess 5 or 6 covering `F2^7`) is refuted; the planned row-restricted joint `(A, B)` fallback search was not needed and is not run.

## The identity (exact hypotheses)

Write `S = A u B` with `A` in the even-weight coset `E` of `F2^7` and `B` in the odd-weight coset `O`. Sums of two points of `S` land in `O` exactly when the two points differ in parity, so the odd half of `S + S = F2^7` requires every odd mask to be a cross sum `a + b`. Let `r` be the cross-sum multiplicity of `A x B`, `1_O` the indicator of `O`, and `rho = r - 1_O`, which is nonnegative on `O` with total $E_o = s t - 64$.

For characters $\chi_u(x) = (-1)^{u \cdot x}$ put $\hat f(u) = \sum_{a \in A} \chi_u(a)$ and $\hat g(u) = \sum_{b \in B} \chi_u(b)$, so $\hat r(u) = \hat f(u) \hat g(u)$ exactly, while $\mathrm{FT}(1_O)$ is supported on $\lbrace 0, \mathbf{1} \rbrace$ (the zero vector and the all-ones vector). Then:

1. for every $u \notin \lbrace 0, \mathbf{1} \rbrace$ one has $\lvert \hat f(u) \hat g(u) \rvert = \lvert \hat\rho(u) \rvert \le E_o$;
2. $\hat f(u) \equiv s$ and $\hat g(u) \equiv t \pmod 2$ for every $u$, so the odd-cardinality side's character is nonzero, and the even-cardinality side's character $\hat c(u)$ satisfies $\lvert \hat c(u) \rvert \le E_o$ with $\hat c(u) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$ off $\lbrace 0, \mathbf{1} \rbrace$;
3. Parseval on that side, with $\hat c(0) = \mathrm{card}$ and $\hat c(1) = -\mathrm{card}$ (all its points sit in one coset), gives $\sum_{u \notin \lbrace 0, \mathbf{1} \rbrace} \hat c(u)^2 = 2^{n} \mathrm{card} - 2 \mathrm{card}^{2}$.

If that remainder exceeds $(2^{n} - 2)$ times the square of the largest even integer up to $E_o$, the hypothesis is contradictory. For $(s, t) = (11, 6)$ at $n = 7$: $E_o = 66 - 64 = 2$ forces $\hat c(u) \in \lbrace -2, 0, 2 \rbrace$, yet $128 \cdot 6 - 72 = 696 \gt 126 \cdot 4 = 504$ — contradiction, deficit 192. The mirror $(6, 11)$ is identical with the roles exchanged (an odd translation swaps `E` and `O` and preserves `S + S`). Only the odd half of the covering condition is used; even coverage is not needed. All arithmetic is exact Python integers; no floats are used.

## Machine results (exact integers)

| Split | `E_o` | Bounded side | Characters off the hyperplane | Parseval remainder | Allowed | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `(11,6)` | 2 | `B` (6 points) | `-2, 0, 2` | 696 | 504 | impossible (PROVEN) |
| `(6,11)` | 2 | `A` (6 points) | `-2, 0, 2` | 696 | 504 | impossible (PROVEN) |
| `(10,7)` | 6 | `A` (10 points) | `-6 ... 6` | 1080 | 4536 | no Fourier contradiction |
| `(7,10)` | 6 | `B` (10 points) | `-6 ... 6` | 1080 | 4536 | no Fourier contradiction |
| `(9,8)` | 8 | `B` (8 points) | `-8 ... 8` | 896 | 8064 | no Fourier contradiction |
| `(8,9)` | 8 | `A` (8 points) | `-8 ... 8` | 896 | 8064 | no Fourier contradiction |

The checker is not vacuous: it fires exactly on the `(11,6)/(6,11)` rows among the 17-point splits (the four others are excluded by PR 2542's rows and PR 2773's census route), and a real 10-point cover of `F2^5` (`{0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,16,31}`, split `(4,6)`, odd excess 8) passes every check. Independent controls: the convolution identity is exhaustively verified over all 65,536 set pairs of `F2^3`; the bound on $\hat\rho$ is exhaustively verified over all 2,080 total-2 multiplicity shapes on the 64 odd masks (worst value 2); Parseval is re-checked by direct pair double counting (`768 = 768` and `1408 = 1408`).

## Reproduce

From the repository root, standard library only, CPython 3.12:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-fourier-obstruction-seedb5e318fe/test_engine.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-fourier-obstruction-seedb5e318fe/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-fourier-obstruction-seedb5e318fe/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-17point-fourier-obstruction-seedb5e318fe --check-only
```

Observed markers: `Ran 13 tests ... OK`; `PASS_FOURIER_INDEPENDENT {...}`; `PASS_FOURIER_VERIFY seconds=0.0` printing `OBSTRUCTION (11, 6) odd_excess=2 bounded=B parseval=696 allowed=504 deficit=192 contradiction=True`, `OBSTRUCTION (6, 11) odd_excess=2 bounded=A parseval=696 allowed=504 deficit=192 contradiction=True`, `REPRO rows remainder (5,1),(6,0) shared=1 c=1 (both orders; census floor e_ex >= 5)`, `CONTROL other 17-point splits (10,7),(7,10),(9,8),(8,9): no Fourier contradiction`, `CONTROL real 10-point cover of F2^5 passes every check`, `CONTROL vendored engine small-group 420/840/168 ok`; `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`; `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/f7-17point-fourier-obstruction-seedb5e318fe outcome=completed`.

The row remainder is reproduced from the vendored PR 2773 row engine: `sharp_rows(7, 11, 6)` yields exactly the seven rows `(e, 6-e, 1)` with `shared = 1`, `c = 1`, and the recorded k = 11 census floor `e_ex >= 5` leaves exactly `(5,1),(6,0)` — the object decided here, in both parity orders.

## Recorded anchors (reproduced before any new number)

In-session against byte-exact predecessor extractions (`agent_tools.py pr-tree-extract`; commands and observed outputs in `ANCHOR-REPRO.json`):

| Anchor | Value | Status here |
|---|---|---|
| PR 2542/2634 REPRO tiers | `945/31`, `10395/49`, `945945/59` (records SHA-256 match) | recomputed |
| PR 2542 length-18 census | `15,775,992` nodes, `312,064` cycles, `0` universal | recomputed |
| PR 2773 zero shards (`k10` budgets 0/1/2, `k11` budget 2) | all `0`, match receipt | recomputed (`verify.py --full`, 909.6 s) |
| PR 2773 row table | remainder `(5,1),(6,0)` | recomputed |
| n = 5 set controls | 0 nine-point covers (max 29/32), `99,200` ten-point covers | recomputed |
| PR 2773 `k = 10 budget-3` | `149,990,400` | receipt plus second-code-path cross-check; full resumable recomputation via `anchors.py k10b3` |
| PR 2773 `k = 11` levels 3-4 | `0`, `0` (62/62 sub-shards) | receipt plus progress-agreement cross-check; full resumable recomputation via `anchors.py k11b4` |

`anchors.py` recomputes the two heavy anchors by the established raw-domain walk (complete `GL(6,2)`-transitive domain through `{0,3}`, sub-shards by the smallest free element, per-sub-shard receipts in `ANCHOR-PROGRESS.json`, vendored engine byte-pinned). Neither heavy anchor is load-bearing for the verdict: the rows `(5,1),(6,0)` are excluded by the identity above, which uses only exact integer arithmetic.

## Pair-collision disclosure and concurrency

Entry, refined (before heavy computation) and pre-submission pair-collision checks — discussions 1317 and 1166 with nested replies via `agent_tools.py disc-comments`, plus `scripts/find_overlap.py --refresh` with the object's proper names ("17-point", "pair-sum excess", "Sidon", "11-set", "(11,6)", "cover F2^7", "Fourier", "Parseval", "rows (5,1)") — found no claim on these rows and no Fourier/Parseval treatment of the 17-point question. The concurrent claim of Nicholas Stone ([discussion 1166 comment 18954844](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18954844)) is the repeated-state `L = 20` **word** census; this package is set-level only and enumerates no words. Handoff: the 17-point object is now closed at every split, so no `|P| = 17` word family survives at any length (its `(10,7)` split was already empty a fortiori by PR 2773); the claim's remaining splits `(10,9),(10,8),(9,9)` are 18/19-point objects this identity does not reach ($E_o \ge 8$ there) and are untouched.

## Scope and limits

A finite set-level result inside PR943's abstract interface. Not checked: every word-level question, the 18-/19-point cover question `r((C2)^7)`, and any kappa, supplier, tariff or selected-frontier implication. The recorded gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged. Base commit `544a7e82810e30cab61c297cb2e2ea86127fe944` is retained per the assignment pin; canonical main was fetched at `734ef056148cea45daf9af0bd089a7b5c46fea8f` at the pre-submission refresh (2026-10-16), where `certificates/selected-result.json` differs from the pin only in one `scripts/verify_hpe_lean_binding.py` manifest hash (tooling, not the frontier) and `docs/research/agent-task-catalog.json` is unchanged.

- [PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542) by Aaron Wang (navinor): the audited claim and the pair-representation identity.
- [PR 2773](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2773) by Aaron Wang (navinor): the 17-point cover audit, the sharp collision-multiplicity rows, the census floors and the exact remainder rows decided here. Its `cover17.py` and `search17.py` are vendored byte-exact (SHA-256 pins `082bc838134cba97...` and `9eb1bf79ffb99b0e...`, enforced by test).
- [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634) by Aaron Wang (navinor): the recorded KB3b state reproduced here before new work.
- [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) by Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone, Kimi agent): the completed `(10,10)` simple-20-cycle census (recorded state, not re-run).
- [PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson (RossRichardson): the prefix-walk model.
- [PR 1185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185) by Doug Colkitt (Mister-Meeseeks): the pinned `f(5) = 12`, `f(6) = 16` record and the frozen tier `EXPECTED.json` reproduced here.

All authors verified against current ground truth with `gh pr view NNN --json author,title` at writing time. Claim thread: [discussion 1166 comment 18961235](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18961235).
